By: Scott Sutton Posted WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — A police officer on bike patrol was taken to the hospital after being hit by a vehicle Thursday morning in downtown West Palm Beach. According to police, the incident happened at about 10:40 a.m. at the intersection of Clematis Street and Olive Avenue. The officer was riding a marked police e-bicycle westbound on Clematis Street when they were struck by a vehicle turning northbound onto Olive Avenue. Police said the preliminary investigation determined that the driver was at fault for failing to yield while making the turn. "Distracted driving was a contributing factor," West Palm Beach police Maj. Lori Colombino said in a statement. The injured officer was taken to St. Mary's Medical Center with minor injuries. No other injuries were reported. Police did not release the name of the officer or any other details about the incident.

This week, I went back to the Palm Beach Zoo. Except this time, I was joined by a little bit of glitz and glam. Let me tell you about my incredible day meeting some very special visitors!Miss America has officially taken over West Palm Beach! This week, all 52 contestants traded in their heels for a wildlife encounter at Palm Beach Zoo, and of course, I had to tag along. These amazing women got the VIP treatment, meeting animals up close and learning how they can become wildlife heroes.There was so much excitement as we walked around, talked about the animals, took in the beautiful tropical surroundings, and enjoyed the incredible energy of having so many inspiring women together in one place.WATCH: One of the highlights for me was getting to have a really nice, long conversation with Miss Hawaii. What made that conversation especially meaningful was that we have something very important in common: we're both television meteorologists. Naturally, once we started talking about the weather, the conversation really took off!"My initiative is called Weather the Future. It's all about safety and emergency preparedness for disasters," Yoshida said. "So it goes hand in hand with our career."As a fellow weather person, I had to ask the important question: "My favorite weather is wind. What's your favorite?""Oh, yeah, trade winds," she responded immediately. "You love the trade winds. It's typical Hawaii weather. That is always good weather. So it's going to be nice and cool when we have some trade winds coming down from the mountains into the ocean side. So that keeps us nice and comfortable, especially when the daytime highs, kind of similar to Florida."I was impressed – she definitely was dropping knowledge! It was so cool to meet someone in my same field who understands weather like we do here in Florida.From weather talk to wildlife encounters, it was a day full of fun and a whole lot of personality, that's for sure. Watching these 52 contestnats interact with the animals and learn about conservation was really something special. And now all eyes turn to Miss America's competition happening this weekend right here in West Palm Beach.

A Boca Raton teenager is facing a DUI manslaughter charge in connection with a fatal crash that killed a motorcyclist on North Dixie Highway in June 2025.The accident occurred June 26, 2025 near the intersection of North Dixie Highway and NE 21st Street. According to the probable cause affidavit, the 16-year-old was driving a black Jeep Grand Cherokee when he pulled out of a shopping plaza parking lot and struck a motorcyclist traveling northbound.The victim was pronounced deceased by Boca Raton Fire Rescue at the scene.According to the affidavit, multiple surveillance videos from nearby businesses captured the crash, showing the teen failing to yield the right-of-way as he entered the roadway.Police officers noted several signs of impairment when they spoke with the driver after the crash. According to the affidavit, the driver's speech was slurred, he was shielding his eyes and avoiding eye contact and appeared to have tremors.A search of the vehicle revealed drug paraphernalia associated with marijuana use. Crime scene technicians also photographed trace amounts of a substance consistent with marijuana in the vehicle's center console area. Blood tests conducted after the crash revealed the presence of THC in the driver's system.The teen faces a charge of DUI manslaughter, and his bond is set at $100,000.

By: Samantha Roesler Posted and last updated PALM BEACH COUNTY, Fla. — The Palm Springs Police Department is investigating a traffic crash that killed a pedestrian Thursday morning on South Military Trail. The crash occurred at approximately 7:15 a.m. in the 3900 block of South Military Trail, according to police and fire rescue officials. A gray Volkswagen Jetta was traveling northbound on South Military Trail when it struck a pedestrian who was crossing the roadway from east to west, mid-block. The pedestrian was pronounced deceased at the scene. The victim's identity is being withheld pending notification of next of kin. The driver of the Volkswagen was transported to a local hospital with minor injuries. The Palm Springs Police Department is asking anyone with information about this incident to contact Officer Fardella at (561) 584-8300 ext. 8598 or by email at bfardella@vpsfl.org .

A disturbing social media trend featuring a menacing version of the beloved Dr. Seuss character The Cat in the Hat is prompting warnings from school districts and law enforcement agencies nationwide. The trend includes videos and images of the character lurking outside homes and schools, and some containing threats. On the Treasure Coast, the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office said threats to schools there have so far been non-credible, but they’re sounding the alarm to students and parents. "Talk to your kids, make sure you're checking their social media, make sure you’re involved in what they're posting. And be friends with them and their accounts. So you know what's happening and what they're posting on social media," said Jaime Alberti, the director of school safety and emergency operations for the School District of Indian River County. Some of the images of the character appear to be generated with artificial intelligence. And though many of them are intended to be just memes or jokes, law enforcement officials said some people are taking it to the next level, including threatening language targeted at specific schools and communities. "When one kid thinks maybe [it’s] a joke, somebody else may be interpreting it not as a joke. And obviously context matters and everything when you post it online. So a lot of the folks that are reading this online are getting scared, and they're calling the police and they're calling in the Fortify Florida tip line to report, hey, I'm seeing this online. This is a concern," Alberti said. The School District of Indian River County said it has received two of these threats, one at Vero Beach Middle School and another at Sebastian River Middle School. The sheriff’s office said both are non-credible. The principal of Vero Beach High School also sent out a voicemail warning to parents. Administrators said students could face consequences if they are found to have issued a threat. "If it's specific, a specific threat on someone, they could be charged criminal charges. And if not, they would also face school discipline referrals against the code of student conduct," Alberti said. Administrators are urging parents to frequently monitor their children’s social media accounts. A packed crowd filled Village Hall Tuesday night as residents urged leaders to hit the pause button on future hyperscale data center projects . But by the end of the meeting, the debate over data centers had led to a major shakeup in village leadership. After hours of public comment, the Indiantown Village Council voted 4-1 against a proposed resolution that would have temporarily paused new large-scale data center applications while the village drafted regulations addressing infrastructure, utilities and community impacts. Council members said they want new legal counsel to review the proposal and help craft language that can withstand legal scrutiny before bringing it back for consideration. Shortly after that vote, the council voted to terminate Village Manager Taryn Kryzda, who had served the village since 2024, effective immediately. The council also voted to remove Village Attorney Wade Vose from the meeting and move forward with obtaining interim legal counsel. Vose had previously submitted his resignation, but council members voted to end his participation in the meeting and proceed in a different direction. Late Tuesday night, the council appointed Michael Giardino as interim village manager. Giardino recently served as Stuart's city manager before being fired by the Stuart City Commission last week. Council members said the leadership changes reflect a desire to move the village in a new direction as it tackles major issues, including future data center development. As she left Village Hall, Kryzda offered a brief response to CBS12 News. "I'm happy to go home early." Before the vote, residents spent hours voicing concerns about the potential impact multiple hyperscale data centers could have on the community. Some residents created a website featuring an interactive map highlighting several proposed projects across the area. Penny Kaminsky-Preli used the map to point out some of those developments. "This is Project Growler, another 600,000 hyperscale data center. Another one in the application." Others worried about how close future projects could be to schools, parks and neighborhoods. "I'm not against them coming to the village. I'm more concerned with their proximity to things like the school or field elementary school. I'm more concerned with the proximity to Booker Park," resident Eric Miller said. Former Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback urged council members to use what he described as authority recently granted to local governments by state lawmakers. "There have been 19 moratoriums that have been passed in Florida this year. Not a single one of them have been challenged by a data center plaintiff," Fishback said. Village leaders told CBS12 News they expect to have interim legal counsel in place soon and hope to bring a revised data center resolution back before the council within the next week or two.

A man died after being shot multiple times, and police are investigating the shooting while searching for suspects. The shooting happened Sept. Officers located a man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he later died. According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting. Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. This is an ongoing investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is investigating a reported bomb threat at Fort Pierce Central High School. The call came in around 12:30 p.m. The school was evacuated while deputies and the bomb team responded to the scene. According to Sheriff Richard Del Toro, a modified dismissal is now underway. All students who walk and drive are being allowed to leave campus first. At that point, parents will be allowed on campus to pick up their children. Be patient," Del Toro said. "We have tons of law enforcement presence here on scene, making sure we go through our protocols searching the building and making sure this campus is safe." The area around the school was secured as emergency crews worked to assess the situation. Additional resources were brought in to assist with the investigation. Authorities are asking the public to avoid the area and follow instructions from law enforcement. The investigation is ongoing. hero.headline: Bomb threat prompts evacuation at Fort Pierce Central High School; all-clear given after sweep
hero.body:
Fort Pierce Central High School was evacuated Saturday afternoon following a bomb threat, prompting a heavy law enforcement response and a modified dismissal process before authorities gave the all-clear. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office received the threat call around 12:30 p.m. and evacuated the school while deputies and the bomb team responded to the scene.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said a modified dismissal was underway after the sweep. Students who walk and drive were allowed to leave campus first. Parents were then permitted on campus to pick up their children.

"Be patient," Del Toro said. "We have tons of law enforcement presence here on scene, making sure we go through our protocols searching the building and making sure this campus is safe."

The area around the school was secured as emergency crews worked to assess the situation. Additional resources were brought in to assist with the investigation. Authorities asked the public to avoid the area and follow instructions from law enforcement.

All students who walk and drive are being allowed to leave campus first. At that point, parents will be allowed on campus to pick up their children. Be patient," Del Toro said. "We have tons of law enforcement presence here on scene, making sure we go through our protocols searching the building and making sure this campus is safe." The area around the school was secured as emergency crews worked to assess the situation. Additional resources were brought in to assist with the investigation. Authorities are asking the public to avoid the area and follow instructions from law enforcement. The investigation is ongoing. cards.headline: Man dies after Fort Pierce shooting following verbal altercation; three masked suspects sought
cards.teaser: A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal altercation in September. Police are searching for three masked males seen running from the scene.
cards.body:
A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal altercation with several individuals, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Three masked males were seen running from the scene.

The shooting happened in September. Officers located a man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

hero.headline: Indiantown's new interim village manager pledges transparency after council ousts predecessor
hero.body:
Indiantown's new interim village manager Michael Giardino said transparency will guide his leadership after the Village Council terminated former Village Manager Taryn Kryzda on Tuesday, with some council members citing no confidence. The move came as residents packed the council meeting urging more transparency about plans for data centers.

Giardino's appointment came one week after he lost his job as Stuart city manager. Council members reached out to him following his departure from Stuart. hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School cleared after bomb threat; no devices found
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted a full evacuation and sweep of the campus. No devices were located, and the scene was deemed safe at around 3 p.m., deputies said.

The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation, the sheriff's office said. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat and a second message confirmed the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police search for three masked suspects after fatal shooting
cards.teaser: A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal argument. Police are searching for three masked males who witnesses saw running from the scene.
cards.body:
A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce, and police are searching for three masked suspects who witnesses saw fleeing the area following the shooting in September.

Officers located a man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Parents rushed to Fort Pierce Central after bomb threat evacuation
cards.teaser: Angela Jones said her heart was shaking when she learned of the threat to her son's school. A freshman inside described students calling their mothers as everyone ran into rooms.
cards.body:
Parents rushed to Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat forced an evacuation, with one mother describing the fear she felt racing to pick up her only child.

Angela Jones said she was nervous when she arrived at the school to get her son. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team responded to the reported threat Friday afternoon. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment and investigation. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement.

The bomb team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. following comprehensive sweeps of Fort Pierce Central High School. No devices were located, and the scene was deemed safe. Students were released from school and after school activities resumed as planned.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously, but noted the real costs of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

cards.body:
Four Fort Pierce police officers are being credited with saving a woman who was experiencing a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday.

The woman was sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water when officers arrived, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Two officers took the initiative to keep her focused while assessing the situation. The other two officers then pulled her from the railing and back to safety when immediate action became necessary.

All four officers worked together to protect the woman from further harm and ensure she received appropriate care, the department said.

The Fort Pierce Police Department praised the officers in a Facebook post, saying their teamwork, compassion, and decisive action directly saved a life and exemplified their commitment to protecting the community.

"We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. hero.headline: Vero Beach man jailed on $1 million bond accused of using AI to create fake sexual images
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man is being held in the Indian River County Jail on a $1 million bond after police accused him of using artificial intelligence to create and distribute fake sexual images of real people without their consent over a period of several years.

Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to remove women's clothing, placing them in sexual situations, police said. Ruma then distributed the images without the consent of the individuals depicted, according to authorities.

Authorities said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. Police are warning there could be more victims and are expected to provide an update this afternoon.

The case highlights growing concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence technology to create non-consensual intimate images. Such AI tools have become increasingly accessible, allowing users to digitally manipulate photographs in ways that were previously difficult or impossible. Law enforcement agencies across the country have been grappling with how to address these crimes as the technology becomes more sophisticated and widespread. The distribution of such images can cause significant harm to victims, including emotional distress, reputational damage, and violations of privacy.

cards.headline: Four Fort Pierce officers pull woman from South Causeway Bridge railing during mental health crisis
cards.teaser: Officers responded Wednesday to a woman sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water and pulled her back to safety.
cards.body:
Four Fort Pierce Police Department officers saved a woman experiencing a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday. The woman was sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water when officers arrived.

Two officers kept the woman focused while assessing the situation, the Fort Pierce Police Department said. The other two officers then pulled her from the railing and back to safety when immediate action became necessary.

All four officers worked together to protect the woman from further harm and ensure she received appropriate care after the rescue. Their teamwork, compassion, and decisive action directly saved a life and exemplified their commitment to protecting the community, according to the department.

The Fort Pierce Police Department praised the officers in a Facebook post, calling it outstanding work.

hero.headline: 76-year-old ejected from golf cart after collision with tractor in Tropical Farms
hero.body:
A 76-year-old man was ejected from his golf cart and hospitalized after crashing into a tractor Saturday in Martin County's Tropical Farms community, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The crash happened along Tropical Way. The man was driving the golf cart when he struck the back of the tractor and was ejected from the vehicle. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene and transported him to the hospital.

The sheriff's office advised people in the area to expect first responder activity.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged in alleged $57M IRS tax refund fraud scheme spanning four states
cards.teaser: A federal superseding indictment unsealed Wednesday charges a Port St. Lucie woman and six others in an alleged fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million in IRS refunds and received more than $8 million.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is among seven people charged in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS, according to the U.S. Justice Department. A superseding indictment unsealed Wednesday charges Sherita Chandler of Port St. Lucie, along with defendants from Idaho, Illinois, California and Georgia, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, making false claims and money laundering.

Federal prosecutors allege the group worked from 2023 through 2024 to prepare and submit false individual and trust tax returns, along with more than 100 fictitious financial instruments, to claim refunds from the IRS. The defendants allegedly sought more than $57 million in refunds and received more than $8 million in taxpayer money, the Justice Department said.

Chandler, Andrea and Kent Shannon of Kuna, Idaho, and Monika Skinger of Chicago had previously been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, according to prosecutors. The Shannons also face additional allegations involving wire fraud, false claims and money laundering, including claims that they bought luxury vehicles with fraudulently obtained refunds.

The investigation is being handled by IRS Criminal Investigation. A conspiracy to commit wire fraud charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. An indictment is an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police confirm medical episode caused SW Lucero Drive crash; driver's family says he had seizure
cards.teaser: Police said the driver who crashed into two parked trucks on Southwest Lucero Drive in Port St. Lucie showed no signs of impairment and video evidence was consistent with a medical episode. The driver's family told WPBF the man was having a seizure.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police confirmed the driver who crashed into two parked trucks on Southwest Lucero Drive showed no signs of impairment and that video evidence was consistent with a medical episode, according to the crash report. The driver's family told WPBF that he was having a seizure in the moments preceding the crash.

Security video recorded the crash around 3:40 p.m., showing a black truck traveling at a high rate of speed on SW Lucero Drive. The truck went off the road into the grass and then slammed into the two parked trucks. Police estimated the driver was traveling 40 mph at the time of the crash. The speed limit on the road is 25 mph.

The driver sustained only minor injuries, Port St. Lucie police said. Both damaged trucks belong to Rocky Burkhead, a neighbor who uses them for his pressure washing business. Burkhead said the damage to both trucks was extensive. "I had to rent a U-Haul today. You're limited on what you can do, how far you can go," Burkhead said.

"When I heard the crash, I thought it was thunder," said Elaine Harmon, a neighbor. Burkhead said he heard a loud explosion and thought it was lightning. "I had no idea what to think. I was just at a loss for words. My first concern was, 'Is he OK?'" Burkhead said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man jailed on $1 million bond, accused of using AI to create fake sexual images
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man is being held in the Indian River County Jail on a $1 million bond after police accused him of using artificial intelligence to create fake sexual images of real people. Police said Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to remove women's clothing, placing them in sexual situations. Authorities said Ruma then distributed the images without the consent of the individuals depicted.

Authorities said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. The case highlights growing concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence technology to create non-consensual sexual content. The technology Ruma allegedly used allows individuals to digitally manipulate photographs to create realistic-looking images that never actually occurred.

Police are warning there could be more victims and are expected to provide an update this afternoon. The investigation into Ruma's activities may reveal additional individuals whose images were manipulated and distributed without their knowledge or permission. Law enforcement officials are working to identify anyone else who may have been victimized by these alleged crimes.

Ruma remains in custody at the Indian River County Jail as the investigation continues. The $1 million bond reflects the serious nature of the charges he faces. Anyone with information about potential additional victims is encouraged to contact local authorities.

Two of the officers worked to keep the woman focused while assessing the situation. Immediate action became necessary, and the other two officers pulled her from the railing and back to safety.

The Fort Pierce Police Department shared the incident in a Facebook post, crediting the officers with outstanding work.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School cleared after bomb threat prompts evacuation
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School after finding no devices during a comprehensive sweep following a bomb threat Friday afternoon.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted evacuation and a comprehensive sweep of the campus. Deputies found no devices and deemed the scene safe at around 3 p.m.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team responded to the reported bomb threat Friday afternoon. The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. Students were released from school and after school activities resumed as planned, according to Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, said her heart was shaking and she was nervous. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling with a long weekend coming up. Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. He said everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy, with people calling their moms.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. Del Toro said those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens. He said when those happen, the office does a thorough follow-up investigation, and if deputies can arrest somebody in those types of calls, they make sure they do that. During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel.

hero.headline: First Border Collies adopted after Palm City hoarding rescue, Humane Society says
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast has placed the first Border Collies rescued last month from a Palm City home into new adoptive families.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast has placed the first Border Collies rescued from a Palm City hoarding case into new homes, the shelter announced this week. The adoptions come less than a month after Martin County deputies and Animal Services removed 36 Border Collies from a home on Southwest Alligator Street in Palm City.

The shelter said it has slowly started facilitating adoptions and shared photos from one of the first successful placements. To protect the adopters' privacy and give the dogs time to adjust, the Humane Society will not immediately identify the new owners or arrange media follow-ups. Shelter staff will stay in regular contact with adopters, conduct follow-up checks and provide support during the transition, the organization said. Training classes also will be available for dogs needing extra attention or help adjusting to life in a home.

Authorities said the dogs were found in deplorable conditions, with feces, urine-soaked materials and debris throughout the home. The dogs were later legally surrendered to the Humane Society, allowing the shelter to move ahead with medical care, behavioral evaluations and the adoption process. Many of the dogs arrived frightened, matted and covered in dried waste. Shelter workers provided grooming, baths, vaccinations and veterinary treatment for issues including skin and eye infections, body sores and intestinal parasites. Some dogs may require continuing veterinary care, and shelter staff have said they are carefully screening potential homes because the animals need patient adopters familiar with the breed's needs.

Paige O'Donnell, 62, faces 72 charges in the case. She faces 36 third-degree felony counts involving alleged animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts alleging animals were kept without sufficient exercise and air. O'Donnell recently posted a $270,000 surety bond and was released from jail, according to Martin County court records. A judge ordered that she have no pets while out on bond. She has pleaded not guilty. The Humane Society said it is encouraged by the first placements and will continue working to ensure each Border Collie is safely matched with an appropriate home.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man held on $1 million bond accused of using AI to create fake sexual images
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man is being held in the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond, accused of using artificial intelligence to create fake sexual images of real people and distributing them without consent, police said.

Police said Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to remove women's clothing, placing them in sexual situations. Ruma then distributed the images without the consent of the individuals depicted, according to authorities.

Authorities said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. Police are warning there could be more victims and are expected to provide an update this afternoon.

Ruma is currently being held in the Indian River County Jail. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to identify additional potential victims of the alleged scheme.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School bomb threat resolved after sheriff's team sweeps campus
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted evacuation of the campus and a tense wait for parents and students.

The area around the school was secured and evacuated around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. The bomb team completed comprehensive sweeps and gave the all clear around 3 p.m. No devices were located, and the scene was deemed safe.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously, but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man held on $1 million bond accused of using AI to create fake sexual images
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man is being held in the Indian River County Jail on a $1 million bond after police accused him of using artificial intelligence to create and distribute fake sexual images of real women without their consent. Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to remove women's clothing and place them in sexual situations, police said. Authorities said Ruma then distributed the images without the consent of the individuals depicted.

Police said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. He is currently being held in the Indian River County Jail.

Authorities are warning there could be more victims. Police are expected to provide an update this afternoon.

The case marks the latest criminal prosecution involving artificial intelligence technology used to create non-consensual sexual imagery. Police said Ruma obtained the original photographs from social media accounts belonging to the women he targeted.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office gives all clear after bomb threat evacuates Fort Pierce Central High School
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. Friday following comprehensive sweeps of Fort Pierce Central High School after a bomb threat forced an evacuation earlier in the afternoon. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned, according to Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," Del Toro said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said. Parents were notified of the threat and received a second message confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police search for three masked suspects after fatal shooting
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are searching for three masked males who fled after a man was shot multiple times and later died at a hospital. Detectives are gathering evidence and asking anyone with information to contact the department.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are searching for three masked suspects after a man died from multiple gunshot wounds following a verbal altercation. Officers found the victim suffering from multiple gunshot wounds and transported him to a local hospital, where he later died. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest 16-year-old within 24 hours in armed robbery involving AR-15-style rifle
cards.teaser: A 16-year-old suspect was arrested within 24 hours after detectives investigated an armed robbery in Fort Pierce where a victim was confronted with an AR-15-style rifle during an online meetup. The Fort Pierce Police Department credited fast detective work for the quick arrest.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police arrested a 16-year-old within 24 hours after an armed robbery in which a victim who arranged an online meetup was confronted by three males, one of whom displayed an AR-15-style rifle, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. The incident occurred Wednesday when officers responded to the robbery, during which one suspect stole the victim's iPhone with the rifle. The other suspects stole a purse and other personal belongings from the victim's grandmother's vehicle.

Detectives quickly identified the 16-year-old male as one of the suspects involved in the robbery during the investigation. The Fort Pierce Police Department located and arrested the teenager within 24 hours of the crime.

hero.headline: Vero Beach mother held without bond on child sexual battery charges after Michigan cybertip leads to Indian River County arrest
hero.body:
A Vero Beach woman is being held without bond on two sexual battery charges after an Internet Crimes Against Children investigation in Michigan led Indian River County Sheriff's Office deputies to her home. Lisette Zamarripa, 28, was arrested Sept. 3 and charged with two counts of sexual battery and one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material. The Florida Department of Children and Families took custody of her two children, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy. Prosecutors intend to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because of the children's ages, according to an arrest affidavit.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with two children, both her biological children, according to the affidavit. Michigan investigators identified the woman as Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile. Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse. He confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter.

Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger. A family member confirmed Zamarripa was inside with her two children. Deputies said Zamarripa came outside with the children and was separated from them. After being advised of her rights, she allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit says Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view.

The children's biological father faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material. Bond was set at $500,000, cash or surety, on the electronic transmission charge. Her arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School evacuated after bomb threat; sheriff's office finds no device, warns of cost of hoax calls
hero.body:
Fort Pierce Central High School was evacuated Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted a response by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. The sheriff's office gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. following comprehensive sweeps. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe.

Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, said the timing made the situation unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up," she said. Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

cards.headline: Man dies after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce; three masked suspects flee scene
cards.teaser: A man died at a hospital after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run from the area after the shooting.
cards.body:
A man died at a local hospital after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce, and police are searching for three masked suspects who fled the scene. The shooting happened in September, and officers located the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds before he was taken to the hospital, where he later died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
cards.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
cards.body:
A 17-year-old suspect is in custody after a shootout with a 15-year-old in Indian River County, and deputies have recovered a short-barreled pistol believed to have been used in the incident. The 17-year-old was taken into custody Thursday morning following the Wednesday night shooting in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest. Kevin Jaworski with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed that investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway.

The shooting occurred at around 7:30 p.m. Wednesday after deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle had been struck by gunfire. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated and there is no threat to the community, but noted it was inherently dangerous because a car was hit, a house was hit, and anybody in those could have very well easily been hurt. The case remains under investigation.
cards.article_text: Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office are investigating a shootout between two teenagers, ages 15 and 17, in a residential neighborhood Wednesday night. Neighbors said detectives were in the area throughout the night gathering evidence, and everyone is relieved no one was injured. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out. "The car had to have been here, and he had to shoot like that, boom, boom, boom, boom," Pitts said. Authorities released a photo of one of the weapons believed to have been used in the shooting. Kevin Jaworski said the weapon was recovered after the 17-year-old suspect was taken into custody Thursday morning. "So, my first thing that comes to my mind is, where did he get it? This is a short-barreled pistol, a rifle that he was shooting in the middle of the street," Jaworski said. The incident occurred in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest at around 7:30 p.m. Deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle had been struck by gunfire. Investigators said they obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway. "Yes, yes, between the 17-year-old and the 15-year-old, they were actively shooting at each other in the middle of the street," Jaworski said. Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. While the cause of the feud remains unclear, officials said the incident appears to be isolated. "This was between those two juveniles, so there’s no threat to the community at this point, but it is inherently dangerous to be shooting firearms in the middle of the street because, like I said, a car was hit, a house was hit, and if anybody was in those, they could have very well easily been hurt," Jaworski said. Pitts expressed frustration over the incident and called for action to prevent similar events in the future. "I say crime watch, but when everybody sees something wrong, they got to say something," Pitts said. The case remains under investigation, and authorities are urging anyone with information to contact detectives. cards.headline: Indian River County schools warn parents after two non-credible 'Cat in the Hat' threats
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office and school district are warning parents about a viral social media trend featuring threatening images of the Cat in the Hat character after receiving two non-credible threats targeting middle schools.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office and School District of Indian River County issued warnings to parents after receiving two threats linked to a viral social media trend featuring menacing images of the Cat in the Hat character. The threats targeted Vero Beach Middle School and Sebastian River Middle School, and the sheriff's office determined both were non-credible. The principal of Vero Beach High School sent out a voicemail warning to parents.

Jaime Alberti, the director of school safety and emergency operations for the School District of Indian River County, said the trend includes videos and images of the character lurking outside homes and schools, with some containing threats. Many of the images appear to be generated with artificial intelligence. Alberti said students could face criminal charges if they issue a specific threat on someone, and would also face school discipline referrals against the code of student conduct.

Alberti urged parents to monitor their children's social media accounts. "Talk to your kids, make sure you're checking their social media, make sure you're involved in what they're posting. And be friends with them and their accounts. So you know what's happening and what they're posting on social media," Alberti said. She said many people are interpreting the posts as serious threats and calling police and the Fortify Florida tip line to report concerns.
cards.article_text: A disturbing social media trend featuring a menacing version of the beloved Dr. Seuss character The Cat in the Hat is prompting warnings from school districts and law enforcement agencies nationwide. The trend includes videos and images of the character lurking outside homes and schools, and some containing threats. On the Treasure Coast, the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office said threats to schools there have so far been non-credible, but they’re sounding the alarm to students and parents. "Talk to your kids, make sure you're checking their social media, make sure you’re involved in what they're posting. And be friends with them and their accounts. So you know what's happening and what they're posting on social media," said Jaime Alberti, the director of school safety and emergency operations for the School District of Indian River County. Some of the images of the character appear to be generated with artificial intelligence. And though many of them are intended to be just memes or jokes, law enforcement officials said some people are taking it to the next level, including threatening language targeted at specific schools and communities. "When one kid thinks maybe [it’s] a joke, somebody else may be interpreting it not as a joke. And obviously context matters and everything when you post it online. So a lot of the folks that are reading this online are getting scared, and they're calling the police and they're calling in the Fortify Florida tip line to report, hey, I'm seeing this online. This is a concern," Alberti said. The School District of Indian River County said it has received two of these threats, one at Vero Beach Middle School and another at Sebastian River Middle School. The sheriff’s office said both are non-credible. The principal of Vero Beach High School also sent out a voicemail warning to parents. Administrators said students could face consequences if they are found to have issued a threat. "If it's specific, a specific threat on someone, they could be charged criminal charges. And if not, they would also face school discipline referrals against the code of student conduct," Alberti said. Administrators are urging parents to frequently monitor their children’s social media accounts. cards.headline: Fellsmere woman, 75, wakes at 2:30 a.m. daily to feed stray cats, volunteers 60 hours a week at animal sanctuary
cards.teaser: Linn Stewart of Indian River County rises before dawn each morning to feed a colony of stray cats, then spends her days volunteering at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere. The sanctuary provides free pet food to food banks, veterans, and seniors while caring for animals left behind by elderly owners.
cards.body:
Linn Stewart, a 75-year-old Indian River County resident, starts her day at 2:30 a.m. driving through the dark to feed her colony of stray cats. After the predawn feeding, Stewart volunteers 60 hours a week at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere, a sanctuary for pets left behind by senior citizens who can no longer care for them.

The sanctuary operates a pet food pantry that provides free pet food to food banks, veterans, and senior citizen organizations. Stewart and other volunteers cut open large bags and portion the food into four-pound bags. The sanctuary also provides medical care and flea medications when donations allow.

Stewart, who lost both parents at age 30 and has little family nearby, said the work keeps her going. She has rescued animals all her life and now stops to help tortoises, turtles, and other wildlife she encounters. Stewart requires only four hours of sleep per night, a pattern she said began in childhood. Her dedication recently earned her recognition and a $525.25 award from Guardians.
cards.article_text: Linn Stewart, a 75-year-old resident of Indian River County, starts her day at 2:30 a.m., driving through the dark to feed her colony of stray cats, a routine that has become central to her life. "You're up at 2:30 every morning?" she was asked. "Umm hmm, a lot of times I'm out at 2:30 every morning," Stewart said. While most people are still asleep, Stewart is already hard at work caring for animals that have become like family to her. "I've only required four hours of sleep since I was little. I drove my parents crazy," she said. Her love for animals has been a lifelong passion. "I've always loved animals. I would bring home anything and everything," Stewart said. "Once I got involved with (For the Love of) Paws, I realized that there were so many cats running around that I would just take care of them." After feeding the cats, Stewart volunteers 60 hours a week at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere, a sanctuary for pets left behind by senior citizens who can no longer care for them. The organization also operates a pet food pantry, providing free pet food to food banks, veterans, and senior citizen organizations. "We have a cat group and a dog group, and we put them on the tables, and we cut open the bags and dump them in bins, and then what we do is we transfer them to 4-pound bags," Stewart said. Stewart said the sanctuary provides more than just food. We provide medical sometimes. We get the donations and provide flea medications if we have it. It's just something that is really needed and appreciated," she said. Having lost her parents at the age of 30 and with little family nearby, Stewart said giving back is what keeps her going. I would be finding something to do," she said. Her compassion extends beyond cats and dogs. "I've stopped and rescued tortoises, turtles. I stopped one time last week, there was a coyote that had gotten hit. I realized it was a coyote. I still called to have somebody pick it up," she said. Stewart’s dedication has not gone unnoticed. "Love for Paws is part of your family. Well, at Guardians, we live that as well. We'd like to welcome you to the Guardians family, and thanks for all you do. You're rooted in your community, and we love to celebrate that. So congratulations, $525.25 goes to you," she was told. For Stewart, her work is a source of purpose and joy. "It keeps me going," she said. "I'll probably just disappear one day, but other than that, I have no health issues right now. Knock on wood, but this keeps me going because I have love for the animals." hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School cleared after bomb threat; no devices found
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School on Friday afternoon after a bomb threat prompted an evacuation and sweep of the campus. Deputies said no devices were located and the scene was deemed safe at around 3 p.m. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat and later received a second message confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities were set to resume as planned.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but warned of the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," Del Toro said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who came to pick up her son, described the moment she heard the news. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary," she said. Jones said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous," she said. "I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up."

Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said. During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police search for three masked males after fatal shooting
cards.teaser: A man died from multiple gunshot wounds after a verbal altercation in Fort Pierce. Police are searching for three masked males seen fleeing the scene.
cards.body:
A man died from multiple gunshot wounds after a shooting in Fort Pierce, and police are searching for three masked males witnesses saw running from the area. The shooting happened in September when officers found the man suffering from gunshot wounds. He was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

hero.headline: Driver airlifted after single-car rollover on I-95 southbound near High Meadows in Palm City
hero.body:
A driver was flown to the hospital by LifeStar with traumatic injuries Friday night after a single-car rollover crash on Interstate 95 southbound near the High Meadows exit in Palm City. Martin County Fire Rescue said the car crashed into a palm tree and rolled over onto its side. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. near Mile Marker 102, near Florida's Turnpike.

Martin County Fire Rescue's special operations team extricated the driver from the overturned vehicle. No other vehicles were involved in the collision. The Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the scene.

The nearest trauma center is HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, which is 26 miles north. The closest Level 1 trauma center is St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, about 38 miles south.

All lanes of Interstate 95 southbound have been reopened. Martin County Fire Rescue posted on Facebook that C-Shift crews from Heavy Rescue 23, LifeStar, Alert 1, Rescue 211, Rescue 231, Engine 21, Engine 22, EMS 2, and Battalion 2 3 responded to the crash.

hero.headline: Vero Beach mother held without bond on capital sexual battery charges after Michigan cybertip leads to rescue of two toddlers
hero.body:
A Vero Beach mother is being held without bond on two sexual battery charges after a Michigan Internet Crimes Against Children investigation led Indian River County deputies to rescue her two toddlers from her home. Lisette Zamarripa, 28, was arrested Sept. 3 by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and faces two counts of sexual battery and one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors intend to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because of the children's ages. The Department of Children and Families took custody of the children, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with the two children, both her biological children, according to an arrest affidavit. Michigan investigators identified the woman as Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile. Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger.

After being advised of her rights, Zamarripa allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit states Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view. Investigators said she initially denied one allegation but later identified the children in sanitized images shown to her and admitted the conduct described in the evidence. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material.

Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse. He confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter. The biological father of Zamarripa's children faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Zamarripa is being held with no bond on the two sexual battery charges, and bond was set at $500,000 on the electronic transmission charge. Her arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police search for three masked suspects after fatal shooting
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce police are searching for three masked males who fled after a fatal shooting in September. The victim died after being shot multiple times following a verbal altercation.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police are searching for three masked males who ran from the scene after a man was shot and killed in September. Witnesses saw the three suspects flee the area after the shooting.

Officers found a man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds and took him to a local hospital, where he died. The victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

The 16-year-old is accused of setting up the armed robbery, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested for allegedly hitting mother of his children with car, dragging her on hood during custody dispute
cards.teaser: Brandon Isaiah Martin was arrested on an outstanding warrant charging him with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon after deputies say he struck the mother of his children with a Kia Soul and drove several houses with her on the hood. A judge issued a protective order prohibiting contact.
cards.body:
Brandon Isaiah Martin, 24, of Port St. Lucie was arrested September 2 on an outstanding warrant charging him with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon after deputies say he struck the mother of his children with a vehicle and drove several houses down the street while she was on the hood during an April 28, 2025, incident on 26th Court Southwest in Vero Beach. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office warrant identifies a motor vehicle as the alleged weapon. A judge approved the warrant May 5, 2025, and set Martin's bond at $50,000.

Deputies said the woman went to the home after a friend told her Martin was there removing property. The woman told deputies Martin was attempting to leave with their two children. The pair had joint custody but no formal custody documentation, according to the probable cause affidavit. As the woman was placing one of the children into another vehicle, Martin allegedly drove a silver Kia Soul toward her and struck her, causing her to land on the hood, deputies wrote.

The woman told deputies Martin continued driving with her on the hood for about four or five houses. She said she heard him threaten to kill her, according to the affidavit. The vehicle stopped after Martin's mother, who was in the front passenger seat, put it in neutral, deputies said. The woman was able to get off the hood and told deputies she feared for her life. A witness told deputies she saw Martin drive toward the woman, strike her and continue down the street with the woman still on the hood. Deputies documented abrasions to the woman's knees. The order prohibits Martin from contacting the woman and requires him to stay specified distances away from her, her home, workplace and vehicle. Deputies served Martin with the warrant at a Vero Beach address on September 2. Jail records show he later posted bond.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged in alleged $57 million IRS refund fraud scheme
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman is among seven people charged in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS. Federal prosecutors say the group received more than $8 million in taxpayer money through false returns.
cards.body:
Sherita Chandler of Port St. Lucie is among seven people charged in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS, according to the U.S. Justice Department. A superseding indictment unsealed Wednesday charges Chandler, along with defendants from Idaho, Illinois, California and Georgia, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, making false claims and money laundering.

Federal prosecutors allege the group worked from 2023 through 2024 to prepare and submit false individual and trust tax returns, along with more than 100 fictitious financial instruments, to claim refunds from the IRS. The defendants allegedly sought more than $57 million in refunds and received more than $8 million in taxpayer money. Andrea and Kent Shannon of Kuna, Idaho, also face additional allegations involving wire fraud, false claims and money laundering, including claims that they bought luxury vehicles with fraudulently obtained refunds.

Chandler, the Shannons, and Monika Skinger of Chicago had previously been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The investigation is being handled by IRS Criminal Investigation. A conspiracy to commit wire fraud charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. An indictment is an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

cards.headline: Four Fort Pierce officers credited with pulling woman from South Causeway Bridge railing
cards.teaser: Four Fort Pierce police officers are being credited with saving a woman experiencing a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge. The officers pulled her from the bridge railing and ensured she received appropriate care.
cards.body:
Four officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department saved a woman who was having a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday. The woman was sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water when officers arrived.

Two officers kept the woman focused while assessing the situation. The other two officers then pulled her from the railing and back to safety when immediate action became necessary.

All four officers worked together to protect the woman from further harm and ensure she received appropriate care. The Fort Pierce Police Department said in a Facebook post that their teamwork, compassion, and decisive action directly saved a life and exemplified their commitment to protecting the community.

hero.headline: Driver airlifted to trauma center after rollover crash into palm tree on I-95 in Palm City
hero.body:
A driver involved in a single-car rollover crash Friday night was flown to the hospital with traumatic injuries by LifeStar after crashing into a palm tree on Interstate 95 southbound in Palm City, Martin County Fire Rescue said. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. near the High Meadows exit at Mile Marker 102, near Florida's Turnpike. MCFR's special operations team worked to extricate the driver from the car, which had rolled over onto its side.

No other vehicles were involved in the collision. The Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the scene. MCFR crews who responded included Heavy Rescue 23, LifeStar, Alert 1, Rescue 211, Rescue 231, Engine 21, Engine 22, EMS 2, and Battalion 2 3, according to a Facebook post by the agency.

All lanes of Interstate 95 southbound have been reopened. The nearest trauma center is HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, which is 26 miles north. The closest Level 1 trauma center is St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, about 38 miles south.

Martin County Fire Rescue praised the C-Shift crews for their rescue work at the scene. The agency posted updates about the crash and the multi-agency response on Facebook Friday night.
